authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Events and Time - Formal Execution.md, §VII (The Convergence Theorem) + spec §4J.4 step 3 (declared dimension kind)
note: Shapiro, Preguiça, Baquero & Zawirski (2011); Kleppmann (2017, ch. 5). ★★ The payoff of the row: LWW attaches to a snapshot dimension AUTOMATICALLY from its declaration, and delta-accumulation on one becomes a TYPE ERROR — the rule stops being remembered and starts being checked.
★★_the_type_error_is_proven_by_a_compile: The strongest available form, and it is executed rather than described: `SnapshotDim` carries a ```compile_fail``` doctest that calls `.add(...)` on a balance read off an SMS. `cargo test --doc` runs it and it PASSES — which means the code genuinely does not build. There is no `add` on the type, so delta-accumulation is **unspellable** rather than refused at run time. ★ And the honest completion: a kind declared in a *spec* with an update arriving off a *wire* cannot be a Rust type error, so `DimensionSchema::check` refuses it there too. Both halves are needed, and claiming the compile-time one covered the declared-in-data case would be the dishonest version of this.

reconciliation_before_building.★_vclock::Dimension_was_EXTENDED_not_for: The vector-clock slice already shipped a `Dimension` with `Snapshot`/`Contested` for merge resolution. §VII needs a third kind — `Accumulating` — so the variant was added to **that** enum rather than a parallel one being invented beside it. Adding it forced `MergeResolution::resolve`'s match open, which turned out to be the useful part.
reconciliation_before_building.★★_and_resolve_became_a_TYPED_outcome_be: `resolve` returned a bare `Vec<Stamped<T>>` meaning two different things (one value = superseded, two = keep both). A third kind would have made it mean three, and a `Vec` that means three things is exactly the remembered rule this row exists to replace. It now returns `Resolved::{Superseded, BothCount, NeedsReconciliation}` — so a contested resolution can no longer be *mistaken* for a snapshot one, and an accumulating one can no longer be picked from. Three call sites were corrected in place.
reconciliation_before_building.★_the_total_order_was_REUSED_not_re_deri: §VII's `(τ, id)` Lamport tie-break already ships on `event::Observation`, with its own tests. `SnapshotDim` wraps it; nothing here re-derives the tie-break, which matters because two observations at equal `τ` stop commuting without it.
reconciliation_before_building.★_and_the_law_checkers_too: `crdt.rs`'s `laws_hold` and `converges` are used to prove the three laws and strong eventual consistency, rather than the laws being restated as bespoke assertions.

divergence.statement: There is no declared dimension kind in apps/api/sustena/ — `snapshot`, `accumulating` and `dimension_kind` are all grep-0 as a declaration. Nothing checks that a delta is not being applied to an observed quantity; §VII's rule is remembered by whoever writes the operator.
divergence.★★_the_counterweight_and_it_is_the_STRON: §VII's own field note is the counterweight and it should be quoted, not paraphrased: *'VOS runs the LWW-by-event-time balance guard live. It was built empirically after out-of-order SMS clobbered a balance — before it had a name. And when the forwarding macro broke silently for a week and manual SMS-export replay carried ingest, balances stayed correct: §VII is why.'* So the LWW-for-snapshot **behaviour** shipped in the reference, correctly, and it shipped **before the theorem was written down about it**. §VII's closing line is exact: *'the convergence theorem is not being proposed to VOS; it is being written down about VOS.'* This row is not bringing a missing behaviour; it is turning a hard-won empirical rule into a checked one.
divergence.★_and_the_snapshot_vs_contested_distinct: Half of the declaration was already here: `vclock.rs`'s `Dimension` shipped with `Snapshot`/`Contested` when vector clocks landed, precisely so a concurrent pair could be resolved correctly. What EVT-10 adds is the third kind, the automatic attachment, and the refusals.

term_by_term.★★ LWW-by-event-time for an observed bal: AT PARITY IN BEHAVIOUR, and derived there first — the staleness guard (§4J.2) is live in the reference.
term_by_term.the (τ, id) total order: RUST-AHEAD in the tie-break specifically. The reference's guard compares event times; with no `t_event` on the record (EVT-5's gap, closed here today) it uses what it has, so an exact tie has no declared resolution there.
term_by_term.★★ the dimension KIND declared: RUST-AHEAD. Nothing anywhere says *this dimension is an observation* or *this one accumulates*; the distinction lives in whoever wrote the operator.
term_by_term.★★ delta-on-snapshot refused: RUST-AHEAD, and this is the row. In the reference it is a convention, correctly followed, and nothing would catch it being broken.
term_by_term.the accumulating kind as an id-keyed ide: RUST-AHEAD. The reference's accumulating quantities (a pocket's `spent`) are raised by plain addition, made safe upstream by `ingest_engine`'s dedup key rather than by the dimension itself — which is a real defence and a different one: it dedupes the MESSAGE, not the apply.
term_by_term.★ contested → merge-CRDT, never LWW: RUST-AHEAD on both sides of the boundary — `crdt.rs`'s OR-set exists here (MUL-10) and has no counterpart there.

the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.snapshot (89 hits, none a dimension kind: ★ Named again for a different reason than in `checkpoint.json`: there almost every hit was `StateAccessor.snapshot()`; here the point is that none of them declares a *kind*. The word is thoroughly used and never for this.
the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.balance_after (real, and genuinely the r: The transducer extracts `balance_after` from an M-Pesa SMS — an authoritative reading of an external quantity, i.e. **exactly a snapshot-valued observation**. It is parsed and carried in `parsed_fields`, and no operator applies it as one. So the *data* for the snapshot kind is already arriving; only the declaration is missing.
the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.dimension (real hits, a different sense): `dim(S)` in the Cynefin/domain work and `state_schema` dimensions in the DSL sense. Neither is §VII's snapshot-vs-accumulating kind.

divergence.what_python_does_have_and_why_it_is_not_: The right behaviour for the one dimension that mattered most, arrived at the hard way and running in production; message-level dedupe that protects accumulations upstream; and the balance reading already parsed out of every SMS. What it does not have is anything that says which kind a dimension is, or that would object if the wrong apply were used.
divergence.the_honest_limits: Five. (1) ★★ THE DSL AUTHORING SURFACE IS NOT BUILT — declaring a kind in a spec is M-DSL's syntax (Phase 4); this row builds the declaration, the attachment and the refusals, and names the authoring surface as the downstream consumer. (2) ★ NO STATE-TREE INTEGRATION — `DimensionSchema` is keyed by path and is not yet wired into `State`/`StateAccessor`, so nothing forces an operator through it; that wiring is real follow-on work and is not claimed. (3) ★ THE CONTESTED KIND REFUSES AUTOMATIC APPLY ENTIRELY, which is deliberate but blunt — a real reconciliation UI or policy is a separate thing, and the refusal is a placeholder for it rather than a substitute. (4) THE ACCUMULATING KIND'S METADATA IS GENUINELY UNBOUNDED — that is §VII's stated price, not a defect, and it is measured rather than hidden; compaction (dropping ids past a watermark) would be a real further row and would need EVT-6 to say when. (5) A DECLARED KIND CANNOT BE CHANGED — redeclaration is refused, because a dimension that changed kind under a running log would invalidate every apply already made to it; a genuine migration path is EDIT/EVT-15 territory.
divergence.when_python_catches_up: These cases become parity vectors unchanged. The cheapest first step is not the checker — it is the declaration: mark `finances.liquid.balance` snapshot-valued, since `balance_after` is already being parsed out of every SMS and thrown away.
divergence.not_a_divergence_in: R1 behaviour. `vclock::Dimension` gained a variant and `resolve` gained a typed return — both additive to the R2 layer, with the three call sites corrected in place. No `Event` change, no operator change, no existing vector's expectations altered.

fixture.why: The household's own two quantities, which happen to be one of each kind: a balance READ OFF an M-Pesa SMS (an observation of an external authority) and a pocket's spend total RAISED BY increments. Plus a shared plan, which is neither.

snapshot.note: ★ the third is a STALE reading arriving late — it must not clobber

convergence_cases.name: ★★_LWW_converges_under_ANY_permutation_and_ANY_repetition
convergence_cases.why: ★★ §VII's corollary, and the one that matters operationally: *'two phones, offline, receiving the same SMS backlog in different orders, land on the same balance.'* Checked with `crdt.rs`'s own `converges`, which folds **every** permutation and then folds every permutation again with each update delivered **twice** — so order-independence and duplication-freedom are both established over the whole set rather than sampled.

convergence_cases.name: the_snapshot_join_obeys_the_three_laws
convergence_cases.why: Idempotent, commutative, associative — the join-semilattice conditions §VII's proof turns on. Checked with the existing law checker rather than restated as three bespoke assertions.

convergence_cases.name: ★_a_STALE_reading_arriving_late_does_not_clobber_the_newer_one
convergence_cases.why: ★ The production failure the reference hit and fixed empirically: out-of-order SMS clobbering a balance. Ordering on `t_event` rather than arrival is what prevents it — the 9999 reading stamped at τ=50 arrives last and loses to the 1150 stamped at τ=200.

convergence_cases.name: ★_an_EQUAL_event_time_breaks_on_the_id_so_the_order_stays_TOTAL
convergence_cases.why: ★ §VII is explicit that `≻` must be total: two observations with equal event time stop commuting without a tie-break, and the merge stops being a join. Reused from `Observation`'s existing `(τ, id)` rather than re-derived, and checked by asserting the join commutes at an exact tie.

convergence_cases.name: ★_snapshot_metadata_is_O(1)_however_many_readings_arrive
convergence_cases.why: ★ One half of §VII's cost argument, as a number rather than a claim: 500 readings later a snapshot dimension still carries exactly one. This is what LWW buys, and it is the reason the theorem prefers it where it is correct.

derived_not_decreed_cases.name: ★★_NAIVE_ADDITION_IS_NOT_IDEMPOTENT_which_is_the_whole_argument
derived_not_decreed_cases.why: ★★ §VII's counter-example, run rather than quoted: `apply(apply(x,δ),δ) = x + 2δ ≠ x + δ`. Under §V's at-least-once delivery that is not a theoretical blemish, **it is a wrong balance**. Written as plain arithmetic in the test because the shipped type deliberately offers no way to do it — which is itself the point.

derived_not_decreed_cases.name: ★★_carrying_the_APPLIED_IDS_makes_it_idempotent_AND_THAT_IS_THE_COST
derived_not_decreed_cases.why: ★★ The other half, and where the rule comes from. Made safe, an accumulation **is** the grow-only counter: a redelivered delta counts once, and the state is byte-identical rather than merely equal in total. The price is that the applied-id map grows with every distinct delta — 200 deltas, 200 entries — against LWW's constant 1. ∴ *'snapshot-authoritative, never accumulate deltas'* is a **consequence** of requiring convergence under at-least-once, out-of-order delivery, not a decree.

derived_not_decreed_cases.name: the_accumulating_join_also_obeys_the_three_laws
derived_not_decreed_cases.why: The id-keyed union is itself a join-semilattice, so an accumulating dimension converges too — just at a metadata cost the snapshot kind does not pay.

type_error_cases.name: ★★_a_DELTA_on_a_SNAPSHOT_dimension_DOES_NOT_COMPILE
type_error_cases.why: ★★ THE ROW. §4J.4 step 3 asks for a type error and this is one — a ```compile_fail``` doctest on `SnapshotDim` that calls `.add(...)` on a balance read off an SMS. `cargo test --doc` runs it and it passes, which means it genuinely does not build. There is no `add` on the type: the mistake is **unspellable**, not caught. *'The rule stops being remembered and starts being checked.'*

type_error_cases.name: ★_a_snapshot_hands_out_NO_HANDLE_that_could_add
type_error_cases.why: ★ The value-level mirror of the compile-time proof: `DimensionValue::as_accumulating()` returns `None` for a snapshot, so reaching an accumulating apply requires first establishing that the dimension **is** accumulating. There is no route from a declared snapshot to a delta.

type_error_cases.name: ★★_a_delta_declared_against_a_snapshot_dimension_is_REFUSED_from_DATA
type_error_cases.why: ★★ The honest completion, and the half a type system cannot reach: a kind declared in a spec, an update arriving off a wire. `DimensionSchema::check` refuses it by name, and **the reason travels with the refusal** — *not idempotent, so a redelivered one would be a wrong balance* — because a caller who is told only *no* learns nothing about why the rule exists.

type_error_cases.name: an_OBSERVATION_against_an_ACCUMULATING_dimension_is_refused_too
type_error_cases.why: The mirror image, which matters because the rule is not *observations are always safe*: replacing a running total with a reading would discard every contribution already counted. Both directions are wrong, and both are named.

type_error_cases.name: an_UNDECLARED_dimension_is_an_error_not_a_DEFAULT
type_error_cases.why: Defaulting to a kind would be the remembered rule again, wearing a different hat — and defaulting to *snapshot* in particular would silently make every unconsidered dimension LWW. The kind must be declared before anything is applied.

type_error_cases.name: ★_a_dimension_cannot_be_REDECLARED_as_a_different_kind
type_error_cases.why: ★ A dimension that changed kind under a running log would invalidate every apply already made to it — the earlier LWW collapses cannot be reinterpreted as increments after the fact. Redeclaring the *same* kind is a no-op; redeclaring a different one is refused, naming both.

scoping_cases.name: ★_declaring_the_kind_is_ENOUGH_the_apply_ATTACHES_ITSELF
scoping_cases.why: ★ The payoff §4J.4 step 3 asks for: the caller declares `snapshot` and never chooses LWW — `DimensionSchema::apply` attaches it. The stale-reading case runs through the schema too, so the guard the reference discovered empirically is here a consequence of one declaration.

scoping_cases.name: ★★_a_CONTESTED_dimension_keeps_BOTH_edits_where_LWW_would_keep_ONE
scoping_cases.why: ★★ §VII's emphatic limit, made side-by-side: *'LWW converges; convergence is not correctness... two genuinely concurrent edits to the same field under LWW means one is silently discarded — the single easiest way to turn a correct theorem into a lost transaction.'* The same two concurrent changes: as a contested dimension both survive through the OR-set; as a snapshot exactly one does. Only one of those is right for a shared plan, and the declaration is what decides.

scoping_cases.name: ★_a_contested_dimension_refuses_AUTOMATIC_APPLY_entirely
scoping_cases.why: ★ Neither an observation nor a delta applies to a contested dimension, and refusing both is the point: any automatic apply is a machine deciding which human was right. Reconciliation goes through the merge-CRDT, which is why `crdt.rs`'s OR-set is the payload rather than a second structure invented here.

scoping_cases.name: the_contested_join_also_obeys_the_three_laws
scoping_cases.why: The OR-set is a join-semilattice too, so a contested dimension converges on the SET of live edits — convergence and correctness kept apart exactly as §VII asks: replicas agree on what is outstanding without anyone's edit being chosen for them.
